speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash in more detail, such as whether it is raised, flat, or blistered, and when it first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash have a "slapped cheek" appearance on the face, and does the body rash look lacy or net-like? Have you noticed any swelling in her hands, feet, or knees?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a prodrome followed by a "slapped cheek" facial rash and a subsequent lacy body rash is classic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
